missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Минута' is the feminine nominative subject. 'Каждая' agrees in feminine gender, and 'важна' is the short adjective stressing its value.
Strategic focus: Accusative of duration. 'Минуту' is the accusative form expressing a span of time. 'Одну' agrees in the feminine accusative, an extremely common polite request.
Strategic focus: Genitive in negation. 'Минуты' is the genitive form required after 'нет', reinforced by 'ни'. A natural way to say one has no time at all.
Strategic focus: Dative object. 'Минуте' is the dative case after 'рад', the thing one is glad about. 'Каждой свободной' agrees in the feminine dative.
Strategic focus: Accusative with 'на'. 'Минуту' is accusative after 'на' to express by how much the train was late. A very common measurement-of-delay pattern.
Strategic focus: Accusative with 'через'. 'Минуту' is accusative after 'через', meaning in one minute from now. A core future-time expression.
Strategic focus: Accusative with 'за'. 'Минуту' is accusative after 'за', expressing the time within which the action was completed. 'Одну' agrees in the feminine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a numeral. After 'две' the noun takes the genitive singular 'минуты'. 'Осталось' is the impersonal verb, a tense countdown phrase.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Минут' is the genitive plural required after 'несколько'. 'В тишине' is the prepositional setting, a quiet narrative line.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after a numeral. After 'пять' the noun takes the genitive plural 'минут'. 'Через' frames the near future, one of the most useful time phrases.
